Discover and inquireStandard3–5 weeks

Inquiry desk with indicative eligibility

Capture loan inquiries from ads, aggregators, the website, WhatsApp and DSAs, ask only what indicative eligibility needs, check it against the lender's published criteria, and route likely applicants to the right owner. It guides; it never decides.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Loan inquiries arrive from campaigns, aggregators, DSAs and WhatsApp in different formats. Many fall outside the lender's serviceable areas or product rules, while good prospects wait hours for a callback and apply elsewhere. Sales staff sometimes over-promise approval or rates, which turns into complaints and mis-selling risk later.

Trigger

A new inquiry from a lead form, the lender's WhatsApp Business number, website chat, an aggregator feed or a DSA submission.

How it runs

  • Capture the inquiry into one queue with source, product interest and the consent shown at that step. AI reads free-text messages for product and amount, and duplicates of existing customers or open applications are merged.
  • Collect a short set of banded answers on a page on the lender's domain: pincode, product, amount range, age band, employment type and income band. No PAN, Aadhaar or bank details are requested at this stage.
  • Check the answers against the lender's published criteria, such as serviceable pincodes, age, minimum income and product limits, and show a plainly worded result with the reason.
  • Route likely applicants to the branch, relationship manager, DSA owner or digital application journey by product and location, with a summary of what was shared.
  • On multi-lender platforms, display every matching offer that partner lenders return, with each lender's name, amount, tenor, APR and charges, without favoring any lender, as the Digital Lending Directions require.
  • Send one approved follow-up template to opted-in prospects who have not applied, then close the inquiry with a reason code.

Human checkpoint

Indicative results never promise approval, a rate or a limit. Credit assessment, bureau checks and the decision stay with the lender's credit team after a full application, and sales staff take over whenever the prospect asks for a person or the case is unusual.

  • Inquiry-to-application conversion by source
  • Share of inquiries outside serviceable criteria
  • Mis-selling complaints traced to the inquiry stage

Discover and inquireStarter2–4 weeks

Compliance-approved content library and distribution

Draft educational posts, newsletters and WhatsApp updates from approved source material, route each one to the compliance officer, and let advisers and agents share only approved, versioned items that carry the required disclosures.

Insurance agencies & brokers · Wealth & investment advisory

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Advisers, agents and POSPs want to stay visible on LinkedIn, Instagram and WhatsApp, but each post can breach advertisement or communication rules through return claims, misleading benefit statements, missing disclosures or ties with unregistered finfluencers. Compliance teams often see material only after it is published, if at all.

Trigger

A topic is added to the content calendar, a product or regulation changes, or an adviser or agent requests a post from the library.

How it runs

  • Plan topics in a shared calendar tied to approved sources: product brochures, Customer Information Sheets, scheme documents, the firm's research notes and regulator investor-education material.
  • AI drafts posts, carousels and newsletter sections only from those sources, adds the required disclosures and flags phrases such as assured returns, best plan or tax-free for review.
  • The compliance or principal officer edits and approves each item; the insurer approves product advertisements by agents and intermediaries, and adviser advertisements go to BASL while SEBI requires prior approval. Approver, version and expiry are recorded.
  • Approved items are laid out in brand templates and scheduled to company pages, newsletters and opted-in WhatsApp lists.
  • Advisers and agents share co-branded versions from the library only; any edit creates a new draft that goes back for approval.
  • Expired items are withdrawn from the library automatically and the archive is kept for audit.

Human checkpoint

Nothing is published or shared without the named compliance approver's sign-off and any approval the insurer or BASL must give. The workflow does not create return or performance claims, recommend specific securities or plans, or engage unregistered influencers.

Apply, verify and decideAdvanced6–10 weeks

Application, KYC and status tracker

Generate the right checklist for each application or proposal, collect documents through a secure page or DigiLocker, track KYC steps, chase what is missing, and keep the customer updated until a person makes the decision.

Lending & NBFCs · Insurance agencies & brokers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Loan files and insurance proposals wait on missing pages, unreadable scans, name mismatches, Video KYC slots and medical requirements. Operations teams chase items over phone and personal WhatsApp, credit and underwriting receive incomplete files, and customers who hear nothing call the branch, DSA or agent, or quietly go elsewhere.

Trigger

A new application in the LOS, a proposal logged in the broker or agency system, or a requirement raised by credit, underwriting or the insurer, read through the system's API or a scheduled export.

How it runs

  • Build the checklist from product rules and applicant type, such as salaried, self-employed, proprietor, company or NRI, and send it with a secure link on the lender's or broker's own domain.
  • Collect documents by upload, or fetch them from DigiLocker or CKYC where the regulated entity uses those routes, showing the purpose of each consent.
  • Classify each document with AI and flag blur, expiry, missing pages and name or date mismatches for an operations officer to confirm.
  • Track KYC status: CKYC record found, Video KYC booked and completed by the regulated entity's trained official, or additional verification needed.
  • Chase missing items on the customer's chosen channel, and alert the file owner when a file ages past its target.
  • Send status updates at each milestone: received, items pending, under review, approved, declined with the main reasons, disbursed or issued.
  • Before a borrower signs, confirm the KFS reached them, and for digital loans log the cooling-off window the lender's board has set.

Human checkpoint

Operations officers verify documents and resolve KYC exceptions. Credit officers, underwriters or the insurer decide every application and record the reasons; the tracker never approves, declines, prices or sets limits.

Apply, verify and decideStandard3–5 weeks

Client onboarding and risk-profiling workflow

Take a new advisory client from the first call to a signed agreement, KYC confirmed with a KRA, and a risk profile the client has reviewed and consented to, with every record kept together for the retention period.

Wealth & investment advisory

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Advisory onboarding involves KYC, an agreement, fee disclosures, a disclosure of how AI tools are used, a risk-profiling questionnaire and the client's consent to the result. Done over email and PDFs, steps go missing, risk profiles are copied from old templates, and producing records for an inspection takes days.

Trigger

A prospect agrees to proceed after the introductory call and the adviser marks them ready to onboard in the CRM.

How it runs

  • Send the agreement, fee terms and disclosures, including how far AI tools are used in the advice, for eSign on the adviser's own portal.
  • Check KYC status with the KYC Registration Agency and guide clients with incomplete or on-hold records through the next steps.
  • Run the adviser's approved risk-profiling questionnaire on a secure page, covering goals, horizon, income, liabilities, experience and capacity for loss.
  • Score answers with the adviser's documented method and flag inconsistencies, such as a short horizon with a high stated risk appetite, for discussion.
  • The adviser reviews the result with the client, finalizes the profile and sends it for the client's consent by registered email.
  • Store the agreement, KYC confirmation, questionnaire, profile, consent and call notes together, with the first review date set from the agreement.

Human checkpoint

The SEBI-registered adviser finalizes every risk profile and suitability judgment and gives all advice. The questionnaire scores and flags; it never assigns a final profile or recommends products. For distributors, the workflow covers onboarding and service, not advice.

Apply, verify and decideStandard3–5 weeks

Onboarding drop-off recovery for apps

Detect where users stall in sign-up, such as KYC, bank linking or mandate setup, identify the likely reason, and send one helpful, consented nudge or route the user to support instead of sending blanket reminders.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Wallets, neo-banking and lending apps lose many users between sign-up and first use. Generic reminder blasts ignore why someone stopped, such as a failed Video KYC call, a PAN-name mismatch or a bank verification error, and they irritate users who have given up or asked not to be contacted.

Trigger

A product event shows that a user has not completed an onboarding step within the agreed time, or that a step has failed.

How it runs

  • Stream onboarding events from the app into an analytics store, with each user's consent and channel preferences attached.
  • Classify the stall: not started, document problem, Video KYC missed or failed, bank verification failure, mandate not set up, or technical error.
  • Send one helpful message for that reason by push, email or an approved WhatsApp template where the user opted in, with a resume link and a support option, within frequency caps.
  • Route repeated failures and technical errors to support with the event trail, so agents never ask the user to start again.
  • Stop all nudges once the user completes the step, opts out or closes the account, and report recovery by step and cohort.

Human checkpoint

Onboarding operations and compliance handle every KYC exception and decide edge cases. Product owners approve every message and frequency cap, and nudges never promise credit, limits or rewards outside approved terms.

Apply, verify and decideAdvanced6–9 weeks

Merchant onboarding and due diligence queue

Collect merchant documents, run checks on PAN, GSTIN, bank account and website, assign a risk tier, and give onboarding officers one queue, so no merchant goes live before due diligence is complete and approved.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Under RBI's September 2025 payment aggregator directions, PAs must complete merchant due diligence before activation, with full KYC for most merchants and contact point verification for small ones, and most also screen websites for prohibited goods and missing refund policies. Manual checks across email, spreadsheets and vendor dashboards slow good merchants and let incomplete files slip through.

Trigger

A merchant submits the sign-up form, a sales partner refers a merchant, or an existing merchant's re-KYC falls due.

How it runs

  • Collect business details and documents by merchant type on a secure onboarding page, with consent and purpose shown.
  • Run verification through approved vendors: PAN, GSTIN, bank account validation, CKYC where available, and Video KYC or contact point verification where policy requires it.
  • Scan the merchant's website or app listing with AI for refund, cancellation and contact policies, and for product categories the PA does not serve, for an officer to confirm.
  • Assign a risk tier from business category, expected volumes and check results, using rules agreed with the risk team.
  • Present the file in an onboarding console where officers approve, request more information or reject; higher tiers go to risk or compliance.
  • Activate only after approval, send the merchant clear status updates, and schedule re-KYC and monitoring by tier.

Human checkpoint

Onboarding officers approve or reject every merchant, and risk or compliance approves higher-risk tiers. Automated checks inform the decision; they never activate a merchant on their own.

Use and serviceAdvanced5–8 weeks

Servicing assistant grounded in approved documents

Answer policy, loan and investment servicing questions on WhatsApp and the website only from approved documents, with the source shown, and hand account requests, complaints and anything uncertain to a person with the context attached.

Insurance agencies & brokers · Lending & NBFCs · Wealth & investment advisory

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers ask the same questions about waiting periods, exclusions, foreclosure charges, statement downloads, nominee changes and capital gains statements. Answers vary by who picks up, wrong answers become complaints, and simple requests wait in the same queue as urgent ones.

Trigger

A customer messages the business's WhatsApp number or website chat, or emails the service inbox.

How it runs

  • Verify the customer through the registered mobile number or an OTP on the business's own page before sharing any account-specific information.
  • Answer general questions only from the approved document set, such as policy wordings, Customer Information Sheets, charges schedules, FAQs and process notes, and show the source.
  • Turn account requests, such as statements, premium receipts, NOCs, foreclosure letters and nominee or address changes, into service tickets with the details captured.
  • Hand over at once for complaints, claims, grievances, bereavement, suspected fraud, any question about what to buy or sell, or whenever the assistant is unsure.
  • Log complaints with their timeline and tell the customer the escalation route that applies, such as the RBI Ombudsman, the Insurance Ombudsman or SEBI SCORES.
  • Review unanswered and low-rated questions each month and update the document set with each document's owner.

Human checkpoint

Service staff own every account change, complaint and exception, and the grievance redressal officer owns escalations. The assistant gives no advice on products, cover, claim outcomes or investments.

Pay and renewStandard4–6 weeks

EMI reminders and respectful collections workflow

Remind borrowers before each EMI, flag mandate bounces the same day, and run overdue follow-up through approved channels within RBI's conduct rules, with hardship cases routed to a trained officer.

Lending & NBFCs · Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Bounced NACH and UPI AutoPay debits surface late, reminders go out from dialer lists that ignore preferences and contact hours, and early-stage overdue customers get the same treatment as wilful defaulters. That raises complaints and conduct risk without improving recovery.

Trigger

A daily sync of installments due in the coming days from the LMS API or export, and mandate presentation results from the sponsor bank or payment gateway.

How it runs

  • Send pre-due reminders in the borrower's language with amount, date and payment options by DLT SMS, email, app notification, or an approved WhatsApp utility template where the borrower opted in, with no offers that would make them promotional.
  • Detect bounced debits the same day and send a factual notice by DLT SMS, email or app notification with a payment link on the lender's domain and charges as set in the loan agreement.
  • Run overdue follow-up by SMS, email, app and calls from 1600-series numbers, since WhatsApp's policy lists debt collection as a prohibited use, and schedule calls only between 8 am and 7 pm, or narrower hours where rules or borrower preferences require.
  • Flag hardship signals, such as job loss, illness or bereavement, and route them to a trained officer to discuss options under the lender's policy.
  • When a recovery agent is assigned or changed, send the borrower the agent's details by SMS and email before any contact, and from January 2027 confirm the agent's certification first.
  • Log every attempt, outcome and recording reference, and report any contact outside the rules to the collections head the same day.

Human checkpoint

Collections officers decide settlements, restructuring, waivers, agent assignment and any legal step. The workflow never threatens, never contacts relatives or references, and never sends legal notices on its own.

Pay and renewStandard3–5 weeks

Renewal reminders for motor, health and life policies

Pull upcoming renewals from the broker system or insurer data, remind customers well before expiry with the insurer's quoted premium, explain what lapsing means for their cover, and route any change of cover to a licensed person.

Insurance agencies & brokers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Renewal dates sit across insurer portals and spreadsheets. A motor policy that lapses leaves the vehicle uninsured and may need a fresh inspection, a health policy not renewed within its grace period can lose continuity benefits, and customers renew elsewhere because nobody reminded them with the right details.

Trigger

A policy enters the renewal window set for its line of business in the broker system or the insurer's renewal data.

How it runs

  • Build the renewal list from the broker system or the insurer's renewal data, through an API or export, with expiry date, the insurer's quoted premium and claims during the year, and check channel consent.
  • Send reminders at agreed intervals by WhatsApp utility template, DLT SMS or email, with the insurer's renewal link and premium, never a figure the system has calculated itself.
  • Explain what a lapse means by line: for motor, cover ends at expiry and a lapsed policy may need inspection; for health, continuity depends on renewing within the grace period in the policy terms.
  • Route requests to change sum insured, add members, switch insurer or port a health policy to a licensed person, with the customer's history attached.
  • Confirm payment through the insurer's channel, deliver the renewed policy document and update the broker system.
  • Give relationship managers a daily list of high-value or at-risk renewals that need a call.

Human checkpoint

A licensed agent or the broker's qualified staff handles every change of cover, insurer switch, portability request and disclosure question. The workflow reminds and informs; it does not recommend cover.

Claims, disputes and alertsStandard4–6 weeks

Claim intimation, checklists and status updates

Help policyholders intimate claims quickly, collect the right documents for each claim type, follow the claim with the insurer or TPA, and explain every status and query in plain language until settlement.

Insurance agencies & brokers

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Customers often intimate claims late, miss documents or misread insurer queries, and the adviser finds out only when the customer complains. Claims desks track many claims across insurer and TPA portals by hand, and delays beyond regulatory timelines go unnoticed.

Trigger

A customer reports an accident, hospitalization, loss or death by WhatsApp, phone, email or the claims form.

How it runs

  • Record the intimation with time, policy and event details, share the insurer's claim helpline and next steps, and alert the claims executive.
  • Help the claims desk register the claim on the insurer or TPA portal within the time limit in the policy terms.
  • Send a checklist for the claim type, such as health reimbursement, motor own damage, theft or a life death claim, with a secure upload link.
  • Check uploads for completeness and legibility with AI and list missing items for the claims executive to confirm.
  • Track status through insurer or TPA APIs or exports where they exist, otherwise from their status emails and the claims executive's updates, and explain each query and milestone in plain language.
  • Alert the claims manager when a claim nears or passes the settlement timeline in IRDAI's master circulars, so it can be escalated with the insurer.

Human checkpoint

The insurer or TPA decides every claim, and surveyors assess losses where required. The broker's claims executive verifies every submission and handles death claims personally; the workflow never predicts or promises an outcome.

Claims, disputes and alertsAdvanced6–9 weeks

Dispute and chargeback operations queue

Bring card chargebacks, UPI disputes and failed-transaction complaints into one queue with deadlines, gather evidence automatically from ledgers and merchants, and give analysts a drafted response to review before anything is submitted.

Fintech & payments

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Disputes arrive through acquirer and card network portals, NPCI's dispute system, merchant emails and support tickets, each with its own reason codes and deadlines. Analysts copy data between tools, evidence requests reach merchants late, and missed deadlines become automatic losses or compensation for delayed failed-transaction reversals.

Trigger

A new chargeback, UPI dispute or failed-transaction complaint arrives from a network portal, the sponsor or acquiring bank, or the helpdesk.

How it runs

  • Normalize each dispute into a case with transaction, reason code, amount, merchant and the response deadline that applies.
  • Pull evidence automatically: ledger and settlement records, authentication results, refund history, delivery or service proof and past disputes.
  • Request missing evidence from the merchant with a deadline and reminders, listing what that reason code needs.
  • Draft a representment summary with AI from the evidence pack for the analyst to edit.
  • The analyst accepts, represents or refunds; failed-transaction reversals and any compensation follow RBI's turnaround time rules.
  • Track deadlines and outcomes by network, reason code and merchant, and pass repeat patterns to the risk team.

Human checkpoint

Dispute analysts decide every acceptance, representment and refund, and finance approves write-offs. Nothing is submitted to a network or bank without an analyst's approval.

Fraud alert triage for analysts

Enrich every fraud or risk alert with customer, device and transaction context, summarize the evidence, prioritize the queue by severity and time sensitivity, and record each analyst decision to improve the rules.

Fintech & payments · Lending & NBFCs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Rules and models raise more alerts than analysts can clear, and each review means opening the core system, device logs, past cases and KYC files. Urgent cases, such as an account takeover in progress or a mule account receiving funds, wait behind low-risk noise, and decisions are rarely recorded well enough to improve the rules.

Trigger

An alert from transaction monitoring, the risk engine or early warning signals on loans, or a fraud complaint received through the cybercrime reporting system.

How it runs

  • Enrich the alert with account age, KYC status, device and login history, velocity, beneficiaries and linked accounts.
  • Summarize the evidence with AI in a fixed format and suggest a priority with reasons, citing the data used.
  • Queue alerts by severity and time sensitivity, and page the on-call analyst for alerts that need action within minutes.
  • The analyst decides: release, contact the customer through a verified channel, hold or block within policy, or escalate to the fraud risk unit.
  • Record the decision and reason, trigger customer messages from approved templates, and pass reportable cases to the officers who own fraud reporting and suspicious transaction reports.
  • Review outcomes weekly with the risk team to retire noisy rules and adjust thresholds.

Human checkpoint

Fraud analysts decide every hold, block, release and escalation. Classifying a borrower account as fraud follows the lender's board-approved process, including the borrower's right to be heard, and fraud reports to the regulator and suspicious transaction reports to FIU-IND stay with the responsible officers.

  • Evidence summary format and priority rules
  • Analyst console with decision logging

Portfolio reviews with SIP and goal check-ins

Schedule reviews from each client agreement, prepare a review pack from RTA and back-office data, flag missed SIPs and approaching goal dates, and remind clients on time, while the adviser makes every recommendation.

Wealth & investment advisory

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

As client books grow, reviews slip, risk profiles age without reassessment, and stopped SIPs or bounced mandates show up weeks later in RTA feeds. Advisers spend review time assembling statements instead of talking about goals.

Trigger

A review date from the client agreement approaches, or the RTA feed shows a missed SIP installment, a SIP nearing its end date or a goal date approaching.

How it runs

  • Pull holdings, transactions and SIP status from the MF back office or RTA feeds where they offer an API or export, or from the client's consolidated account statement.
  • Build a review pack: goal progress, asset mix against the agreed plan, the date of the last risk profile and life events noted since the last review.
  • AI drafts an agenda and summary for the adviser from the pack; nothing reaches the client without the adviser's edit.
  • Invite the client to book a slot through a calendar link, with reminders on the client's chosen channel.
  • For missed or ending SIPs, send a factual reminder and offer a call; no scheme-specific suggestions are sent automatically.
  • After the review, record the advice, rationale and client decisions, and set the next review date.

Human checkpoint

The adviser reviews every pack, gives all recommendations and records the rationale, and risk profile updates are confirmed with the client. Automated messages never recommend schemes, promise returns or present past performance.

Top-up and renewal journeys approved by credit

Find borrowers who meet the lender's policy for a top-up or renewal review, get the credit team's approval for the list and offer terms, and reach consented customers with a fresh, fully disclosed application.

Lending & NBFCs

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Good borrowers leave through balance transfers because nobody offers them a top-up, while ad hoc offer lists built in spreadsheets reach customers in hardship, ignore marketing consent or imply an approval credit never gave.

Trigger

A monthly LMS run for accounts that meet the policy's review criteria, or a borrower's request for more credit or a renewal, such as a gold loan nearing maturity.

How it runs

  • Select accounts by policy criteria, such as repayment track, tenure elapsed and product rules, excluding hardship flags, restructured accounts and open complaints.
  • Send the list and proposed offer parameters to the credit team; only accounts they approve move forward.
  • Reach customers who gave marketing consent through approved marketing templates, 140-series promotional calls or the app, with an opt-out in every message.
  • Capture interest and open a fresh application in the LOS with updated documents, the credit checks the lender's policy requires and a KFS; no limit rises without the borrower's explicit consent.
  • Route each application to credit for the decision and report conversion and decline reasons by segment.

Human checkpoint

The credit team approves the review criteria, every offer list and every final decision. Offers are never presented as pre-approved unless credit has approved them, and no limit is increased without the borrower's explicit, recorded consent.
